title: Quinoa Stuffed Peppers
subtitle: Colorful, balanced, batch-friendly
description: Colorful, balanced, batch-friendly. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Quinoa Stuffed Peppers in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch beef. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Prep pepper boats
steps.instruction: Halve bell peppers lengthwise; remove seeds. Blanch in boiling water 3 minutes; drain cut-side down on towels. Maintain a steady simmer — bubbles should break the surface without a rolling boil that shreds delicate proteins. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Brown beef filling
steps.instruction: Brown ground beef with onion and garlic. Stir in cooked rice, crushed tomatoes, and Italian seasoning; simmer 10 minutes until thick. Target 145°F for steaks, 160°F for ground at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Fill and top
steps.instruction: Mound beef-rice filling into pepper halves on sheet pans. Top with shredded mozzarella. Plan about 12 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 145°F for steaks, 160°F for ground at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 145°F for medium beef, 160°F for ground. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Quinoa Stuffed Peppers onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Scale for larger halls
steps.instruction: When cooking for more than 8 firefighters, split into two pans halfway through so the bottom layer does not overcook while the top waits — duplicate mise en place if you double batches.

steps.title: Bake until tender
steps.instruction: Bake at 375°F 25–30 minutes until peppers are tender and cheese bubbles. Stuffed Peppers slice cleanly if filling is tight — drain excess liquid before baking.

steps.title: Final quality check before service
steps.instruction: Walk the line once before opening service for Quinoa Stuffed Peppers — confirm hotel pans are labeled, backup trays are in the 200°F oven, and thermometers are calibrated. Rookies should ask a senior cook to spot-check the first portion.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Plate Quinoa Stuffed Peppers with sides in separate pans so the crew can mix portions.
Portion bowls on the line with protein visible on top — crew eats with their eyes first.
Keep dressing and crunchy toppings in side bowls so greens stay crisp through second servings.
Line up Quinoa Stuffed Peppers on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Colorful, balanced, batch-friendly. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
mealPrepNotes: Prep mise en place before the shift — Quinoa Stuffed Peppers runs smoother when proteins are trimmed, spices are pre-measured, and hotel pans are labeled before the first tone.
